forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.B.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with bl, sp, sc, sk and ck (sc and sk both say /sk/) in a sentence or conversation (for example black, spoon, school, desk, duck) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match the word to the picture
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.T.mastery: The child chooses the theme word that fits a sentence or picture (for example duster, sweep, matatu, July, shopkeeper, seedling, bandage, chalkboard, calf, left, litter, radio, dance, chores, sick) and does not swap it for a word of the same group. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.mastery: The child listens to a two-step instruction said once (Pick up the duster and give it to Wanjiru) and does both steps in the order given. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: read a page of a graded reader
ENGL.G2.READIN.T1_FLUENCY.READ_ACCURATEL.mastery: The child reads a short Grade 2 text aloud with almost every word right, sounding out new words with the letter-sounds learnt instead of guessing, at a steady speed (about 40 to 60 words a minute is a guide, to confirm by the teacher). Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T1_COMPREHENSION.PREDICT.mastery: The child uses the title, the pictures and what has happened so far to say what will happen next and names the clue. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T1_COMPREHENSION.WORD_FRO.mastery: The child uses the words around a new word and the picture to choose its meaning in this sentence. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: answer the question on the text
ENGL.G2.READIN.T1_COMPREHENSION.DIRECT_Q.mastery: The child finds the sentence that answers who, what, where or when and answers from the text, with the kind of answer the question word asks for. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T1_VERB_TO_BE_PAST_TENS.W.mastery: The child picks was and were from a text and uses was with I, he, she and it, and were with we, you and they and plural nouns: We were at school. The children were happy. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T1_VERB_TO_BE_PAST_TENS.O.mastery: The child picks us, you and them from a text and uses them after a verb or a word like to and with (The teacher called us. Give them the books.), not as the subject. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T1_HANDWRITING.DESCENDERS.mastery: The child picks out g, j, p, q and y as letters whose tails hang below the line, in long words in a text, and spots a word where a tail sits on the line. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T1_HANDWRITING.HANDWRITIN.mastery: The child writes long words with every letter the right shape, tall letters reaching up, tails hanging down, small letters even, and a finger space between words. Evidence rule: the teacher sees it in two pieces of the learner's own work, scored with the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.C.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /tʃ/ (ch), /əʊ/ (long o, as in home, boat), /ʃ/ (sh) and cl in a sentence or conversation (for example chair, soap, dish, clean) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the word after the teacher
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child says words with consonant blends (cl, fl, st, gl, br, cr, dr, fr, gr, pr, tr, sm, sn, sp, scr, spr, str, sw) as one beat with no vowel slipped in, keeps l and r apart, and says sh, ch, th (thin) and th (this) clearly. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: read it happily, read it sadly
ENGL.G2.READIN.T2_FLUENCY.READ_WITH_FEEL.mastery: The child stops at full stops, lifts the voice at a question mark, sounds excited at an exclamation mark and lets the voice and face show what a character feels. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T2_COMPREHENSION.INDIRECT.mastery: The child answers simple how and why questions by joining two clues (Tom smiled and clapped: he was happy) and points to the clue. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which part is like your home
ENGL.G2.READIN.T2_COMPREHENSION.TEXT_TO_.mastery: The child names something in the text that is like his or her own life (I also sweep the house) and something different, keeping to what the text says. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T2_VERB_TO_DO_PRESENT_A.S.mastery: The child picks we, you and they in a text and uses them as the subject (We sweep the house), not us or them, and does not repeat the subject (not My mother she cooks). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T2_VERB_TO_DO_PRESENT_A.V.mastery: The child uses does with he, she and it, do with I, you, we and they, and did for the past, with a plain verb after it: Did you sweep? She does the dishes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T2_HANDWRITING.ASCENDERS.mastery: The child picks out b, d, f, h, k, l and t as letters that reach up, in long words in a text, and spots a word where a tall letter is written short. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /s/, /l/, fl and /eɪ/ (long a, as in train, play) in a sentence or conversation (for example bus, lorry, fly, train) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say a sentence with the word
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.U.mastery: The child uses a new theme word in a short spoken sentence of four or more words, with the right meaning (I travelled by matatu), not a single word. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T3_VERBS_TO_HAVE_OBJECT.V.mastery: The child uses has with he, she and it, have with I, you, we and they, and had for the past: Baraka has a bicycle. We had a matatu ride. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /ŋ/ (ng), /iː/ (long e, as in sheep), st and gl in a sentence or conversation (for example sing, week, star, glad) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the word after the teacher
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child says English vowel sounds so a listener hears the right word: ship and sheep, cup and cap, pull and pool, cot and coat, bird (not bad), with weak vowels short (the a in banana). Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T4_SIMPLE_PAST_TENSE.SIMP.mastery: The child finds past verbs in a text and uses -ed for regular verbs (played, stopped) and the right form for common irregular ones (went, ate, saw), with time words such as yesterday and last month. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: what is wrong with this writing
ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T4_HANDWRITING.HANDWRITIN.mastery: The child chooses the writing with well-formed letters, finger spaces, letters sitting on the line and capitals only where needed, and says what is wrong with poor writing. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T4_HANDWRITING.GL_Y_WORDS.mastery: The child builds theme words with gl and y (glad, glue, July, sunny, January) from letters and spells them correctly. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with nt, sl, -ar (said /ɑː/), nd and nk in a sentence or conversation (for example plant, slow, market, sand, bank) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T5_NOUNS_PLURALS_OF_IRR.I.mastery: The child finds irregular plurals in a text and uses child and children, man and men, woman and women, foot and feet, tooth and teeth, and sheep and sheep in sentences about shopping. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T5_SPELLING.SPELL_GRADE_W.mastery: The child spells common Grade 2 words of three to seven letters (money, shop, buy, garden, water, farmer) correctly and clearly. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.E.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /ɪə/ (as in ear, deer), /θ/ (thin), /ð/ (this), wh (said /w/) and tw in a sentence or conversation (for example ear, thorn, there, wheel, twig) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T6_TENSE_PAST_CONTINUOU.P.mastery: The child picks past continuous sentences from a text and changes the present continuous into the past: I am watering the plants becomes I was watering the plants; they are digging becomes they were digging. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T6_SPELLING.SPELL_TH_WH_T.mastery: The child spells garden words with th, wh, tw and ear (thorn, there, wheel, twig, near) with th, not t or d, and wh, not w or h alone. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with nd, nk, /eɪ/ (cake), /əʊ/ (home) and /aɪ/ (bike) in a sentence or conversation (for example bandage, drink, pain, nose, knife) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T7_COMPREHENSION.CHARACTE.mastery: The child names the people and animals in a story, says one thing about each (kind, brave, careless) and tells the main events. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T7_CONJUNCTIONS.CONJ_OR.mastery: The child picks or in a sentence and uses it to give a choice (Do you want tea or milk?), and answers an or question by choosing one, not with yes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T7_SPELLING.SPELL_NK_ND_A.mastery: The child spells three- to six-letter words with nk, nd and ar (pink, hand, car, park) with both final letters and ar, not a. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.B.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with br, /ə/ (the weak sound at the start of about and the end of teacher), /iː/, /eɪ/ and /əʊ/ in a sentence or conversation (for example brush, teacher, read, table, chalk) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T8_CARDINAL_AND_ORDINAL.C.mastery: The child tells counting numbers (one, two, three) from order numbers (first, second, third) and uses each in the right place: I have two pencils; I was second in the race; first, second, third, fourth, fifth. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T8_CARDINAL_AND_ORDINAL.T.mastery: The child uses these for more than one thing near (these books) and those for more than one thing far (those trees), with a plural noun. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T8_SPELLING.SPELL_VOWEL_T.mastery: The child spells classroom words with br and vowel teams (brush, teacher, read, chalk, table, board) and does not write a long vowel with one letter (red for read). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T9_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.C.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with cr, /ɜː/ (bird, her), /eɪ/, /aɪ/, y said /i/ (happy) and ar in a sentence or conversation (for example cow, crop, bird, hay, sky, puppy, farmer) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T9_COMPREHENSION.SETTING.mastery: The child names the place and time of a story (on the farm, early in the morning) from the words and pictures. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T9_COMPREHENSION.MAIN_IDE.mastery: The child chooses what the whole text is about, not one detail, and says whether it tells a story or gives facts. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T9_COMPREHENSION.RETELL_I.mastery: The child retells three or four events in the order they happened, in own words, using first, next, then and last. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T9_WORD_SETS_GENDER_SET.G.mastery: The child gives and uses gender pairs of the farm and home: cock and hen, bull and cow, ram and ewe, boy and girl, uncle and aunt, king and queen, lion and lioness. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION_THE_COMM.C.mastery: The child finds commas in a text and writes a list of farm things with a comma between items and and before the last (cows, goats, hens and ducks). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /ɪə/, /ə/, /ɜː/, dr, /ɔɪ/ (boy, coin) and /aɪ/ in a sentence or conversation (for example near, turn, drive, point, right) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T10_COMPREHENSION.MENTAL_.mastery: The child uses the describing words to picture a character, place or event and chooses or draws the picture that matches every detail. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T10_PREPOSITIONS.PREPOSIT.mastery: The child picks the target prepositions in an oral text and uses them to describe where things are and where they go: the bird flew over the house; the lamp is above the table; we walked across the road to the shop. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which mark goes at the end
ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T10_PUNCTUATION_THE_EXCL..mastery: The child finds exclamation marks in a text and uses one at the end of a sentence that shows a strong feeling or a warning (Stop! Look out!), not after ordinary sentences. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with fr, /aʊ/ (cow, flower), /ɔː/ (forest, warm) and /ə/ in a sentence or conversation (for example fruit, flower, forest, water) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.READIN.T11_FLUENCY.PHRASE_READIN.mastery: The child reads groups of words together (in the morning / we went / to the forest) instead of stopping after every word. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T11_REGULAR_COMPARATIVE_..mastery: The child finds -er and -est words in a text and uses -er than for two (the river is cleaner than the pond) and the -est for more (the tallest tree), with big, bigger spelt right. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: write a sentence with the word
ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T11_GUIDED_WRITING.WRITE_.mastery: The child writes two or three short sentences about the theme, each with a capital letter, a doing word and a full stop. Evidence rule: two pieces of the learner's own writing marked Meeting Expectations or above on the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with gr, pr, /ɔɪ/, /uː/ (food, computer) and /ʊ/ (book, put) in a sentence or conversation (for example grow, press, toy, phone screen, book) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T12_POSSESSIVE_PRONOUNS.P.mastery: The child finds mine, yours, ours, hers and his in a text and uses them on their own (The phone is mine), his for a boy and hers for a girl, with no apostrophe. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match the word to the picture
ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_WRITING.PICTUR.mastery: The child names the objects in theme pictures in English (radio, phone, computer, television) and writes each name spelt correctly. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: write a sentence about the picture
ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_WRITING.PICTUR.mastery: The child writes one full sentence about what is happening in each picture, using the names of the things in it. Evidence rule: two pieces of the learner's own writing marked Meeting Expectations or above on the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T13_BY_THE_END_OF_THE_SU..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with tr, sm, /tʃ/, /aʊ/ and /juː/ (music, tune) in a sentence or conversation (for example drum, smile, church, crowd, music) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T13_WH_QUESTIONS.WH_QUEST.mastery: The child recognises what, where, when and who questions and asks them in the right order with a question mark: Where is the dance? When did they sing? Who beat the drum? Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T13_GUIDED_WRITING.WORD_O.mastery: The child rearranges jumbled words or phrases into a sentence that makes sense, starting with the capital-letter word and ending with the word before the full stop. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T14_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with /k/ (spelt c, k or ck), sn, sp and u (as in cup and put) in a sentence or conversation (for example cook, kitchen, snack, spoon, run) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T14_ADVERBS_OF_TIME.ADVER.mastery: The child finds the adverbs of time in a text and uses them with the right tense: Tomorrow I will help; Today I am cooking; He came late; We woke up early. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T14_GUIDED_WRITING.RECOUN.mastery: The child writes three or four sentences that tell events, actions or feelings from a story in order, using first, next, then and last, in the past tense. Evidence rule: two pieces of the learner's own writing marked Meeting Expectations or above on the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: circle the words with the sound
ENGL.G2.LISTEN.T15_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears and picks out words with scr, spr, str, sw and st in a sentence or conversation (for example scrub, spray, strong, sweep, stop) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.LANGUA.T15_IMPERATIVES_COMMANDS..mastery: The child picks commands in a text, does what a command says, and gives commands that start with a plain verb (Sit down. Please close the window.), politely. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G2.WRITIN.T15_GUIDED_WRITING.PUNCTU.mastery: The child chooses and uses capital letters (sentence starts, names, I), full stops, question marks and exclamation marks correctly in sentences about caring for others.
